property_summary: Only the current owner can change the owner; after any transfer, the new owner is the address passed to transferOwnership. The bug allows anyone to become owner, so after a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the rule that 'if caller is not owner then owner stays unchanged' is violated.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner can only change if the caller is the current owner; the bug allows anyone to change it.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner should equal the newOwner argument passed to it, but the mutant sets owner to msg.sender instead, breaking this invariant.

After a successful non-revert call to transferOwnership from the current owner, the owner() getter must return the newOwner argument that was passed, but the mutant's transferOwnership sets owner to msg.sender instead, violating this for any call where newOwner != msg.sender.

After a call to transferOwnership(...) that does not revert, the owner must equal the newOwner argument passed, but the mutant sets owner to msg.sender instead, breaking this invariant when newOwner != msg.sender.

For any call to transferOwnership(newOwner) by the current owner that does not revert, the resulting owner must equal newOwner, but the mutant sets owner to msg.sender instead, violating this when newOwner != msg.sender.
After a non-reverting call to transferOwnership(newOwner) by the current owner, the owner must equal newOwner, but the mutant sets owner to msg.sender, violating this when newOwner != msg.sender.
The owner can only be changed by the current owner; the bug allows any caller to change the owner.

The original onlyOwner modifier restricts transferOwnership to the contract owner, while the buggy modifier allows any caller to successfully update the owner; the rule states that a non-owner call to transferOwnership must never change the owner address.
Any call to transferOwnership that does not revert must set the owner to the caller's own address.
After any call to transferOwnership that does not revert, the contract's owner must equal the previous owner; the buggy modifier allows an address other than the true owner to change it.
For any call to transferOwnership, if the caller is not the current owner, the call must revert; the buggy version incorrectly allows a call from address(0x1) to succeed.
For any caller, if transferOwnership succeeds, the new owner must be the address passed; the buggy version makes the caller the owner regardless of the argument.
The owner after any call to transferOwnership must equal the newOwner argument; the bug allows any caller to become owner regardless of the argument.
After any call to transferOwnership, the new owner must be the argument passed to the function; in the buggy contract any caller can become the owner regardless of the argument.

After any call to owned(), the state variable owner remains unchanged in the reference C, but the mutant allows anyone to call transferOwnership and change owner, causing owned() to succeed without the onlyOwner check when owner is changed.
